🤔 Language models

Reasoning model

In simple words

A language model trained to work through a problem step by step before it gives its final answer.

A language model trained to write out its working before it answers: it can break a problem into steps, check them and try another way if something doesn't add up. This makes it better at maths, coding and puzzles, but slower. The first widely used ones appeared in 2024. They still make mistakes, so their answers need checking too.

Example. Like solving a maths problem on scrap paper before writing down the answer, instead of shouting out the first number that comes to mind.

Related words

  • ChatbotA program you can have a conversation with by typing or speaking.
  • HallucinationWhen an AI confidently gives an answer that sounds right but is false or made up.
  • Next-token predictionWhat a language model does: it gives every possible next token a probability, picks one, and repeats.
